purpose: Freeze the current source-bound reconstruction before testing whether the Mendes phallus tradition refers to an original bodily relic, a ritual simulacrum/substitute, or a later theological equivalence.

plutarch_lane: Isis recovers the body parts except the phallus.
A replacement/image of the missing phallus is made for cultic purposes.
This lane does not report later recovery of the original phallus.
egyptian_khoiak_jumilhac_lane: Khoiak day 19: head of Osiris found.
Day 30: Djed raising and completion of the ritual restoration cycle.
mendes_lane: Egyptian Delta traditions assign Osirian relic geography to specific cult centers.
Mendes/Djedet is associated in Egyptian and later Egyptological tradition with a phallus-plus-spine/backbone relic of Osiris.
Banebdjedet is linked with Mendes and with the ba of Osiris.
The existence of this Mendes relic tradition is compatible with, but does not prove, physical survival of an original biological organ.

current_interpretation.user_hypothesis: Osiris may have been restored using a substitute phallus, while an original phallus was found later and preserved in Mendes after Osiris had already departed.
supported_components: Plutarch preserves a missing-phallus plus substitute-image tradition.
Papyrus Jumilhac/Khoiak preserves a later-in-cycle phallus recovery operator on day 25 and/or day 28 depending on variant.
A Mendes/Djedet phallus relic tradition is attested in Egyptian religious geography and later Egyptological discussion.
Papyrus Brooklyn 47.218.84 is a substantially pre-Plutarch Egyptian Delta mythographic source, probably composed under Psammetichus I, and is therefore a key control for Mendes-era traditions.
current_interpretation.unsupported_bridge: No source currently in hand explicitly states: substitute used -> Osiris fully resurrected/departs -> original phallus subsequently discovered -> original hidden/preserved in Mendes for years.

papyrus_jumilhac_khoiak.boundary: variant ritual schedule; not yet demonstrated as a chronological sequel to Plutarch's substitute narrative
papyrus_jumilhac_khoiak.source: UCL Digital Egypt Khoiak comparison / Papyrus Jumilhac tradition

plutarch.boundary: later Greek-language account; no later recovery of original reported in this lane

mendes.boundary: relic identity and material status unresolved: original bodily relic vs simulacrum vs theological cult-object equivalence

brooklyn_47_218_84.date_context: probably reign of Psammetichus I, seventh century BCE, per Dimitri Meeks/IFAO
brooklyn_47_218_84.role: high-priority witness for Delta local myth/relic geography and for testing Mendes tradition before Plutarch

next_gate.frozen_question: Do the earliest Egyptian Mendes/Djedet witnesses treat the Osirian phallus as an original bodily relic, a ritually manufactured substitute/simulacrum, a divine image/container, or a theological equivalence with another cult object?
required_discriminators: Prioritize Egyptian-language or directly translated primary witnesses over later myth summaries.
Separate object labels such as relic/body-part/flesh/member/image/simulacrum/container/emblem from modern paraphrase.
Establish chronology for each witness before constructing a narrative sequence.
Track geographic provenance: Mendes/Djedet, Busiris, Abydos, Heracleopolis, Oxyrhynchus, and Dendera must remain separate until an ancient source explicitly connects them.
A statement that a city 'possesses' a relic does not by itself prove physical authenticity.
A ritual simulacrum does not falsify a separate relic tradition; both may coexist.
Do not infer a post-resurrection timeline unless an ancient witness orders those events.
method_stack: TOPA_SPIDER: provenance-first multi-source crawl with contradiction ledger
5D_SPIRAL: iterate text -> date -> geography -> object ontology -> ritual function and return to contradictory witnesses
BEETLE/GRAZER: deduplicate repeated claims and separate inherited citation chains from independent witnesses
AURA_ORACLE: hypothesis ranking only after source freeze; non-authoritative
TENET/REVERSE: trace late statements backward toward earliest attested source without treating backward reconstruction as evidence
HRaiN/CAT: cluster terms, translations, object identities and local cult relations
NEGATIVE_CONTROLS: seek Mendes texts that omit the phallus or call it explicitly an image/substitute
MATERIAL_GATE: archaeological object claims require catalogue/provenance/context, not mythic identification alone
